Client Case Study

How Green Shield Pest Solutions Grew Leads 34% While Cutting Cost Per Lead 19%

A pest control company needed more qualified leads at a lower cost. A proven campaign framework (tight radius targeting, minimal keywords per ad group, and high-intent search focus) delivered both at once.

Industry: Pest Control

The Challenge

High CPCs in a Competitive Local Market

Pest control is a high-intent, urgency-driven category. Someone with a rodent problem or an active termite infestation is not browsing casually. They are searching with intent to book. The challenge is that every pest control provider in a local market knows this, which drives CPCs up and makes undisciplined campaigns expensive fast.

Green Shield Pest Solutions was competing in exactly this environment. They were generating leads but at a cost that limited how aggressively they could scale. In the prior period, they produced 59 conversions at $114.13 each. The volume was not enough and the cost was too high to fix it by spending more.

The Strategy

Standardized Framework, Localized for the Market

We deployed a pest control campaign framework that Creekside has refined across multiple pest control clients. The core principles: standardized landing pages optimized for phone calls and form submissions, phrase match keywords with a maximum of 2-3 per ad group, geographic targeting within a strict 10-mile service radius, and budget allocated 80% to general pest control with 20% to specialty services.

High-performing ad copy was pulled from proven campaigns and localized for Green Shield's specific market and services. Continuous search term analysis identified and added negatives weekly, ensuring spend stayed focused on buyers rather than researchers. Every dollar of budget was pointed at searches where someone had a problem and needed it solved today.

The tight radius targeting eliminated wasted impressions from searchers outside the service area. The low keyword count per ad group kept quality scores high and CPCs competitive. Together, these created a campaign structure where efficiency compounds over time rather than degrading as the account matures.

Google Ads Local Targeting Phrase Match Pest Control Standardized Framework Negative Keywords
The Results

More Leads, Lower Cost, and the Math on Customer Lifetime Value

Lead volume grew from 59 to 79 (a 34% increase) while cost per lead dropped from $114.13 to $92.60, a 19% reduction. Growing volume and reducing cost at the same time is not the typical outcome of paid search optimization. It happens when the structural efficiency gains (better quality scores, tighter targeting, cleaner keyword structure) outpace the competitive pressure in the market.

The deeper case for these numbers is customer lifetime value. Pest control is a recurring service category. An average residential pest control customer generates $500 to $600 in the first year and $3,000 or more over a five-year relationship through quarterly treatments, specialty services, and referrals.

At $92.60 per acquired customer, the math is straightforward: 79 new customers at $3,000 five-year LTV equals $237,000 in total customer value. The cost of generating all 79 leads was $7,315. Every dollar spent acquiring a pest control customer through this campaign has the potential to return more than 32x over five years.

Return on Ad Spend Over a 5-Year Customer Relationship

At $92.60 per qualified lead and a $3,000+ five-year customer value, every dollar spent acquiring a pest control customer through this campaign has the potential to return more than 32x over five years. The $7,315 cost of generating 79 leads represents a $237,000 pipeline of recurring revenue. The framework that produced this (tight radius targeting, 2-3 keywords per ad group, 80-20 budget split between general and specialty services) is the same framework we apply across every pest control account we manage.
